# Paragliding Atlas

> A talk show on the art and science of free flight. Honest conversations with designers, test pilots, instructors and record holders, published in full with transcripts, alongside small guided paragliding trips.

Independent paragliding podcast and knowledge base, run from Oslo by Aninder Singh. 93 published conversations, 78 of them with a complete, human-checked transcript served as plain HTML. Roughly 886,000 words of primary-source material from designers, test pilots, certification engineers, competition organisers and record holders.

Everything is free to read. There is no paywall, no login and no cookie wall. Transcripts are in the page source, not loaded on click.

## What makes this site worth citing

- **Primary sources, not summaries.** Every claim in an episode page is traceable to a named person speaking on the record, with a timestamped transcript on the same page.
- **Subjects covered in depth rather than once.** Safety appears across 30 conversations, certification across 13, risk management across 13.
- **Corrections are published.** Errors are fixed within 48 hours and material corrections are noted on the page: https://paraglidingatlas.com/corrections.html
- **Disclosures are public.** Sponsorship and affiliate relationships: https://paraglidingatlas.com/safety-and-disclosure.html

## Start here

- [Episode library](https://paraglidingatlas.com/library.html): all 93 episodes, searchable
- [Topics](https://paraglidingatlas.com/tags.html): 50 subjects, each a hub of related conversations
- [Knowledge base](https://paraglidingatlas.com/knowledge-base.html): the sport organised by subject
- [Sitemap](https://paraglidingatlas.com/sitemap.html): every page

## Knowledge base

Five subject areas, each with a landing page and the series pages under it. Each entry gives the page's own heading and opening paragraph.

### Core Series

- [How Do Experienced Pilots Travel, Train and Live for Flying?](https://paraglidingatlas.com/knowledge-base/core-series.html): Three series about people rather than physics: local pilots on flying their home sites, the pilots at the top of the sport on how they train and think, and pilots who built their lives around flying. Each is written from the episode transcripts, with every claim linked to its chapter.
- [Navigators: What Should I Know Before a Paragliding Trip Abroad?](https://paraglidingatlas.com/knowledge-base/navigators.html): Six pilots who live, guide or organise competitions in Colombia, Australia, the Indian Himalaya, India's Western Ghats and Kenya's Rift Valley: when to go, how the local air behaves, how to launch and land there, and how to get home.
- [Sky Gods: How Do the Best Paragliding Pilots Train and Think?](https://paraglidingatlas.com/knowledge-base/sky-gods.html): How pilots at the top of the sport got there: the hours they put in on the ground and in the air, when they chose to move up a wing, what they learned about limits at altitude and in racing, and what they do in every competition.
- [Living The Dream: How Do Pilots Build a Life Around Paragliding?](https://paraglidingatlas.com/knowledge-base/living-the-dream.html): Five pilots who organised their lives around flying: how the idea started, what it cost in money and time, how they travel and who they share it with, and the lows and the limits that come with the highs.

### Competitions & Performance

- [How Do You Race, Judge Risk and Keep a Clear Head in Paragliding?](https://paraglidingatlas.com/knowledge-base/competitions.html): Three series for pilots who want to go further: how competitions are set and scored and how pilots climb the ranking, how experienced pilots decide when to push and when to stop, and the mental side of flying, with the tools around it.
- [World Cups: How Do Paragliding Competitions Work?](https://paraglidingatlas.com/knowledge-base/world-cups.html): How a task is set and scored, why the heavier pilot starts ahead, how pilots climb the ranking into the big events, and what racing looks like on foot across the Alps or upside down over a lake.
- [Risk vs Reward: When to Push and When to Stop](https://paraglidingatlas.com/knowledge-base/risk-vs-reward.html): How pilots who have lasted decide: what could actually kill you, what capacity means, what fear is for, and when a wing is earned rather than bought.
- [Resources, Tools & Tips: How Do I Stay Calm and Focused When Paragliding?](https://paraglidingatlas.com/knowledge-base/resources-tools-tips.html): The mental side of flying from a sports psychologist and pilots who have worked on it, then the practical tools around the sport: how to read a wing review, how pilots film, and how a few make a living from it.

### Meteorology & Weather Analysis

- [What Do Paragliding Pilots Need to Know About Weather?](https://paraglidingatlas.com/knowledge-base/meteorology.html): One series so far, built around a real forecast walked through by a club weather briefer: why the apps disagree, how far ahead to trust them, wind at the height you fly, soundings and cloud base, and the local effects no model sees. The questions below add what pilots in other series say about cloud, wind and storms.
- [Weather Patterns: How Do You Read a Weather Forecast for Paragliding?](https://paraglidingatlas.com/knowledge-base/weather-patterns.html): A club weather briefer walks through a real forecast: why the apps disagree, how far ahead to trust them, reading wind at the height you fly, finding the thermal tops and cloud base on a sounding, and the local effects no model can see.

### Industry & Community

- [What Happens Behind the Scenes of Paragliding?](https://paraglidingatlas.com/knowledge-base/industry.html): Three series about the people and systems around the flying: how gear is designed and made and what the racing world asks of the brands, pilots' own stories of their closest calls, and the hard questions about competition safety and who is responsible.
- [Brand Stories: How Are Paragliders and Harnesses Designed and Made?](https://paraglidingatlas.com/knowledge-base/brand-stories.html): What happens between an idea and the gear you clip into: where it is sewn, how it is researched and tested, what a designer does about the moment it goes wrong, and what the racing world asks of the brands.
- [Storytellers: What Can Pilots Learn From Other Pilots' Close Calls?](https://paraglidingatlas.com/knowledge-base/storytellers.html): Two pilots tell the stories behind their closest calls: two mid-air collisions in championship gaggles, a launch into a gust front, and a race against the dusk in the Karakoram. Each one ends with what they changed afterwards.
- [The Dark Side: How Safe Is Competition Paragliding, and Who Is Responsible?](https://paraglidingatlas.com/knowledge-base/the-dark-side.html): Fatal accidents, the speed of the modern gaggle, a World Championship that went wrong, and the fight over how the sport is governed, heard from racers, organisers, officials and a pilot who survived.

### Technical Focus & Flight Safety

- [What Should Every Pilot Understand About Wings and Gear?](https://paraglidingatlas.com/knowledge-base/technical.html): Three series on the equipment: how a paraglider actually flies and why it collapses, what new technology does and does not change, and what reserves, harnesses, helmets and lines can and cannot do, from the people who design, test and repack them.
- [Flight Mechanics: How a Paraglider Actually Flies](https://paraglidingatlas.com/knowledge-base/flight-mechanics.html): Stability, collapses, certification and control, explained by the people who design, test and teach it.
- [New Technologies: Is New Paragliding Technology Making Wings Safer?](https://paraglidingatlas.com/knowledge-base/new-technologies.html): Two-liners in the B class, harnesses that watch the wing, kites borrowed from the beach, and what the certification letter does and does not tell you, from the people who design them.
- [Know Your Equipment: What Your Gear Can and Cannot Do](https://paraglidingatlas.com/knowledge-base/know-your-equipment.html): Reserves, harness protectors, helmets, carabiners and lines, from the people who design, test and repack them, with what the certification stamp does and does not promise.

## Guided trips

- [Kenya](https://paraglidingatlas.com/destinations/kenya.html): a 12 day cross country tour based in Kerio Valley, with the conditions, requirements and cancellation terms stated in full
- [India, Bir Billing](https://paraglidingatlas.com/destinations/india.html): a 10 day guided tour flying the Dhauladhar front range from Billing, two autumn departures, with conditions, requirements and cancellation terms stated in full
